question: What is the main goal of the Mother-Baby Package in healthcare?

options.A: To focus exclusively on emergency surgical procedures
options.B: To eliminate the need for community health extension workers
options.C: To provide essential health interventions for mothers and newborns together
options.D: To replace routine childhood immunization schedules

explanation: You got this! The Mother-Baby Package bundles care so that both mum and baby get the protection and support they need right from the start. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T005#GNS226_U1_T005_h1)

question: Why do we bundle maternal and neonatal health services together?

options.A: Midwives only work during the first week after delivery
options.B: It is cheaper for hospitals to buy medications in bulk
options.C: Newborns require the exact same medical treatments as adults
options.D: The health and survival of the mother and baby are directly linked

explanation: Spot on! Mum and baby are a team. Treating them together ensures nothing gets missed during these crucial early stages. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T005#GNS226_U1_T005_h1)

question: Which of the following is a major objective of the Mother-Baby Package?

options.A: To reduce maternal, fetal, and newborn mortality rates
options.B: To increase the cost of maternity drugs in local clinics
options.C: To eliminate all traditional birth attendants completely
options.D: To transfer all pregnant women to tertiary teaching hospitals

explanation: Exactly right! Every clinical guideline and care package ultimately aims to keep both mum and baby safe, healthy, and alive. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T005#GNS226_U1_T005_h2)

question: What does 'continuity of care' mean for mothers and children?

options.A: Seeing a different doctor at every single clinic visit
options.B: Stopping medications as soon as the baby is born
options.C: Linking health services seamlessly from pre-pregnancy through childhood
options.D: Keeping a patient admitted in the hospital for the entire nine months

explanation: Great job! Continuity of care means smooth transitions from antenatal care straight through to childhood so no patient falls through the cracks. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T005#GNS226_U1_T005_h2)

question: Why is folic acid given to women before and during early pregnancy?

options.A: To stop excessive bleeding during the third trimester
options.B: To speed up the onset of active labor pains
options.C: To cure maternal high blood pressure permanently
options.D: To prevent neural tube defects in the developing baby

explanation: Correct! Folic acid is a little vitamin with a big job—it protects the baby's brain and spinal cord development in the early weeks. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T005#GNS226_U1_T005_h3)

question: At an antenatal clinic in Nigeria, a pregnant woman receives sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine. What is this for?
explanation: Well done! In malaria-endemic areas like Nigeria, intermittent preventive treatment (IPTp) with SP is a routine lifesaver for pregnant mums. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T005#GNS226_U1_T005_h3)

question: Why is oxytocin given right after a baby is delivered?

options.B: To lower the mother's blood pressure
options.C: To speed up the dilation of the cervix

explanation: Spot on! Oxytocin makes the uterus clamp down firmly, sealing off blood vessels and keeping heavy bleeding at bay. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T005#GNS226_U1_T005_h4)

question: What tool do midwives use during labor to track contractions, dilation, and baby's heart rate on one sheet?
explanation: You got it! The partograph is a nurse's best friend in the labor room for spotting trouble early and keeping track of progress. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T005#GNS226_U1_T005_h4)

question: When should a mother have her very first postnatal checkup after giving birth in a facility?

options.A: Only when the baby falls sick
options.B: When the child is ready for school
options.D: At the end of the sixth week

explanation: Correct! The first 24 hours carry the highest risk for bleeding and newborn issues, so early checks are vital. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T005#GNS226_U1_T005_h5)

question: Which of these is a key nursing check during routine postnatal care?

options.A: Surgically repairing minor perineal tears after 6 weeks
options.B: Administering the BCG vaccine to the mother
options.C: Measuring the child's head circumference daily
options.D: Checking uterine involution and lochia flow

explanation: Well done! Monitoring how the uterus shrinks (involution) and the type of lochia helps you catch postpartum bleeding or infection early. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T005#GNS226_U1_T005_h5)

question: Which vaccine is given to a newborn right at birth to protect against tuberculosis?
explanation: Spot on! BCG is one of those precious birth-dose vaccines given before baby leaves the health facility. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T005#GNS226_U1_T005_h6)

question: What is a major benefit of starting breastfeeding within the first hour of life?

options.A: It helps the baby receive nutrient-rich colostrum and stimulates uterine contraction
options.B: It prevents the mother from experiencing postpartum hair loss
options.C: It replaces the need for any future childhood vaccinations
options.D: It completely guarantees that the child will never catch malaria

explanation: You got it! Early breastfeeding gives baby immune-boosting colostrum and helps mum's uterus contract naturally. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T005#GNS226_U1_T005_h6)

question: Which of the following is NOT a standard nursing duty under the Mother-Baby Package?

options.A: Educating mothers on exclusive breastfeeding practices
options.B: Conducting routine antenatal assessments and checkups
options.C: Administering childhood immunizations according to the schedule
options.D: Performing elective major surgeries in primary health clinics

explanation: Correct! Major surgeries belong in a surgical theater with a doctor, not at a basic primary health clinic. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T005#GNS226_U1_T005_h7)

question: Why is health education such an important part of maternal and child nursing?

options.A: It empowers mothers to recognize danger signs and seek timely care
options.B: It ensures that mothers do not visit traditional birth attendants
options.C: It reduces the need for nurses to document patient visits
options.D: It replaces the need for medical checkups during pregnancy

explanation: Wonderful! When mums know what warning signs to look out for, they can report back early and save lives. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T005#GNS226_U1_T005_h7)

question: What is a major financial hurdle stopping many Nigerian women from accessing maternity care?
explanation: Spot on! Having to pay cash directly at the clinic for every single drug or test discourages many families from getting care. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T005#GNS226_U1_T005_h8)

question: How does task-shifting help improve healthcare in understaffed rural areas?

options.A: By moving specialist obstetricians to every village clinic in the country
options.B: By transferring pregnant patients to urban centers permanently
options.C: By replacing all nurses with automated computer systems
options.D: By training community health workers to safely deliver certain basic health interventions

explanation: You nailed it! Task-shifting bridges the staff gap by letting trained community workers handle basic, safe tasks when professional nurses aren't enough. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T005#GNS226_U1_T005_h8)
